A Langford sequence $L(2, n)$ is a sequence of length $2n$ containing two copies of each integer from $1$ to $n$.
The condition is that the two occurrences of each integer $k$ are separated by exactly $k$ other numbers.
This means if the first occurrence of $k$ is at index $i$ (0-indexed), the second occurrence must be at index $i + k + 1$.
Alternatively, if using 1-based indexing, if the first occurrence is at position $p$, the second is at $p + k + 1$.
The distance between indices is $k+1$.
